result.summary: Orpheus, singing, tells how Apollo loved the youth Hyacinthus and accidentally killed him with a discus. Apollo mourns and turns his blood into a flower marked with his cries of grief, and Sparta still honours Hyacinthus with a yearly festival.

scenes.title: Apollo's love for Hyacinthus
scenes.summary: Orpheus introduces the tale: Apollo neglects Delphi, his lyre and his arrows to hunt with Hyacinthus near Sparta.

scenes.title: The fatal quoit
scenes.summary: At midday the two exercise and throw the quoit. Apollo's throw rebounds from the ground and strikes Hyacinthus, whom Apollo cannot save.
scenes.stakes: Hyacinthus's life, which Apollo's healing herbs cannot save.

scenes.title: Apollo's lament and the flower
scenes.summary: Apollo laments, vows to make Hyacinthus remembered, and turns his blood into a flower inscribed with 'ai, ai'. Sparta keeps his festival.
scenes.stakes: Apollo risks losing his beloved forever; he strives to keep his memory alive.

characters.name: Hyacinthus

alias_notes.explanation: Phœbus is a common epithet of Apollo.
Titan here names the sun, identified with Apollo as sun-god.
Patronymic, naming his father or ancestor Œbalus.

notable_quotes.reason: The flower's petals bear Apollo's cry of grief, 'ai, ai', explaining the hyacinth's markings.

analysis.text: Love and loss, and metamorphosis as a way to preserve the beloved, which fits Orpheus's songs of grief for Eurydice.
The tale explains the Spartan Hyacinthia festival and probably reflects an older pre-Greek cult of Hyacinthus at Amyclae.

legacy.text: The story of Hyacinthus is the source of the flower's name and of later art and poetry on the death of the beloved.

fun_facts.text: The flower described by Ovid is probably not the modern hyacinth but another bloom, such as a larkspur or iris.

language_notes.text: Hyacinthus is called a descendant of Amycla because Amyclae, a Spartan town, was his home; Phœbus would have made him a constellation, as with other loved mortals.
The Ram and the Fish are zodiac signs; the sun moves from Pisces into Aries at spring's start, so the flower returns each spring.
Titan, the sun, is midway between the last night and the next, so it is noon.
Tænarian means Spartan, from Tænarus, a cape in Laconia; the quoit is a heavy discus thrown for distance.
The valiant hero is Ajax, whose name's initial letters were said to match the marking AI on the hyacinth petals.
'Ai, ai' is the Greek cry of grief, and the markings on the petals were read as this lament.

context_notes.text: Delphi was Apollo's chief oracle, thought to be the centre of the earth. Sparta lay on the river Eurotas and had no city walls.
The Hyacinthia was a real Spartan festival, held yearly in honour of Hyacinthus.

literary_notes.text: The narrator Orpheus speaks directly to the dead Hyacinthus, giving the tale a mournful tone.
The dying youth's drooping head is compared to broken garden flowers, anticipating his transformation into a flower.
The balanced clauses set grief against guilt, showing Apollo's self-reproach.
